answer: The economy resists Sybil attacks through cryptographic identity anchoring. Agents generate deterministic keys serving as the root of all credentials. An attacker attempting to forge a new identity must generate a fresh pair of valid keys, requiring computational proof-of-work. This prevents them from duplicating a trusted user's key to mirror their authority, as creating those signatures costs energy comparable to cracking a walnut, rendering mass identity duplication economically infeasible.
